depth_strategy: All 81 universal FBs are included to maximize signal for the rarest class. Cross-domain and specialized classes are oversampled from the 2699 convergent pool to reach 150 and 169 instances respectively, ensuring sufficient representation for the 61-class head. Domain depth is sampled to 600 instances to maintain the corpus's natural majority distribution while providing volume for the 43-domain sigmoid head.
per_domain_coverage: Stratified sampling ensures every one of the 43 domains has at least 15 examples, with high-frequency domains (e.g., graphic design, web & ui) capped at 40 to prevent class imbalance in the multi-label head.
sampling_rules: Source exclusively from the 2699 convergent FBs (2+ sources) to ensure high-quality golden labels.
Enforce a hard cap of 30 examples per discipline to prevent over-representation of large fields like 'design thinking' or 'engineering'.
Prioritize 'universal' and 'cross-domain' FBs for the 61-class discipline head to improve generalization.
Ensure at least 10 examples per discipline to satisfy the minimum threshold for stable LoRA training.
Balance the 43-domain labels such that no single domain exceeds 40% of the total dataset.
authoring_workflow: Query the knowledge base for all 2699 convergent FBs and filter by the 61 discipline labels.
Apply stratified sampling to select 1000 FBs based on the per_depth and per_discipline constraints.
Manually verify the 81 universal and 150 cross-domain examples to ensure label accuracy.
Format the selected FBs into the few-shot prompt template for the DeBERTa-v3-base model.
Split the 1000 examples into 800 training and 200 validation sets with stratified shuffling.
validation: Verify that the macro-F1 for the 61-class discipline head exceeds 0.75 on the held-out 200 validation examples.
Confirm that the 43-domain sigmoid head achieves a macro-F1 of at least 0.70.
Check that no discipline has fewer than 10 or more than 30 examples in the final training set.
Ensure all 81 universal FBs are present in the dataset.
